newsitem.title: ISRAEL: SOCCER-ISRAEL COACH MAKES SQUAD CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ISRAEL COACH MAKES SQUAD CHANGES.

text.p: Israel coach Shlomo Scharf has made five changes in the 20-man squad to face Luxembourg in a European soccer qualifier next week.
The changes, announced on Sunday, followed Israel's shock 2-0 away defeat by Cyprus which dented their chances of qualifying for the World Cup finals in France in 1998.
Scharf decided to drop defenders Felix Halfon, Moshe Glam and Alon Harazi and forward Eli Driks. Talented central defender Gadi Brumer was ruled out through injury.

Scharf has drafted four players from current league leaders Betar Jerusalem, including veteran striker Eli Ohana who was called back despite his retirement from international competition in September 1995.
The other three Jerusalem players are goalkeeper Itzik Kornfein and defenders Assi Domb and Shmuel Levy.
Alon Brumer of Maccabi Tel Aviv, has been also been called in to replace his twin brother Gadi.
Goalkeepers: Bonnie Ginsburg (Maccabi Haifa), Rafi Cohen (Hapoel Haifa), Itzik Kornfein (Betar Jerusalem).

Defenders: Amir Shelah (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Alon Brumer (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Nir Klinger (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Assi Domb (Betar Jerusalem), Shmuel Levy (Betar Jerusalem), Yossi Abuksis (Betar Jerusalem), Alon Hazan (Maccabi Haifa), Tal Banin (Hapoel Haifa).
Midfielders: Avi Nimni (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Eyal Berkowitz (Southampton), Itzik Zohar (Betar Jerusalem), Arik Bennado (Maccabi Haifa), David Amsalem (Betar Jerusalem).
Forwards: Eli Ohana (Betar Jerusalem), Ronnen Harazi (Betar Jerusalem), Haim Revivo (Celta Vigo), Ronnie Rosenthal (Tottenham).
